title: Check out Nachtschacht — my free, turn-based dungeon roguelike for desktop and mobile browsers!
author: Inkompetente_Ente
selftext:
Nachtschacht was developed through an iterative collaboration between me and ChatGPT/Codex. I provided the ideas, creative direction, asset collection, and playtesting feedback. ChatGPT wrote most of the game’s code and also contributed text, content suggestions, and technical solutions.

**My contribution**

I wanted a dark, pixel-art, turn-based dungeon roguelike where characters begin with very weak stats, gain experience, find equipment, and lose everything when they die. I collected third-party graphics, music, and sound packs and specified the direction I wanted for the game.

During development, I played builds and gave feedback on the controls, readability, inventory, camera movement, appearance, and overall feel. For example, I requested keyboard-focused controls, an inventory that stays open when equipping items, a simpler grayscale pixel interface, and an adapted portrait touch interface for mobile.

**Programming and implementation**

I described the desired behavior in plain language, and ChatGPT implemented and revised it in Godot using GDScript. This included procedural dungeon generation, turn-based combat, enemy behavior, equipment, relics, talents, character progression, permanent death, saving and loading, menus, and desktop and mobile controls.

ChatGPT also proposed mechanics and implementation choices. We refined the game through repeated requests, discussion, testing, and changes.

**Writing and game content**

ChatGPT drafted or revised item names, descriptions, tutorial instructions, interface text, and atmospheric writing. It also helped develop equipment effects and balancing, translated the game into English, and assisted with the store-page description.

**Graphics and audio**

Most graphics and audio come from third-party asset packs that I collected. Their sources and licenses are documented in the game and release package.

Some additional artwork—including replacement relic cards, equipment silhouettes, interface elements, and the title logo—was drawn procedurally through code written by ChatGPT. A few short replacement sound effects were synthesized through code as well.

**Testing and release preparation**

ChatGPT wrote and ran automated tests, simulated gameplay, inspected interface layouts, and prepared the Windows and browser exports. I provided feedback from playing earlier builds, while the assistant checked technical behavior and browser layouts.

AI was used during development. The finished game uses conventional game logic for combat, enemies, and procedural generation.
